task: Prairie branch taper and direction correction

humanFeedback.text: The branches don't curve so uniformly. They get thin much faster and the branches don't arc.
humanFeedback.label: Explicit correction request, not candidate approval

hypothesis: The inherited oak Catmull-Rom arches and slow radius falloff cause the repeated bow-shaped limbs. Replace them with unequal straight runs and strong early taper.
implementation: Prairie-only contiguous path deformation, seeded small angular changes, parent-relative attachment transport, faster radius falloff and child radii limited by the supporting parent. Foliage groups move with their owning branch.

review.reviewer: Primary Codex actual hero and close-up screenshot inspection
observations: Uniform branch arches are removed; wood reads as straighter unequal limbs with slender outer tips.
The prominent right specimen no longer has thick bow-shaped lower branches.
Bark detail and connected ring joints remain intact.
Canopy sprays and clump silhouettes remain visibly stylized; no foliage redesign in this pass.

validation.targetedTest: passed, including taper ratios, chord deviation, continuous joints, finite near/far UVs and source preservation
validation.protectedScenes: No shared assets, material code or renderer edits in this pass; scoped to the prairie finishing function.
